levels.label: Emerging
levels.descriptor: Items are grouped vaguely or into one catch-all category, and no specific storage spot or reset rule is written.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: At least three specific categories are named, each with its own storage spot and a written reset rule.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Same as proficient, and the system is physically installed and tested, not only planned on paper.

levels.label: Emerging
levels.descriptor: The one-day test is not actually run, or the report only gives a general impression rather than specific items checked.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: At least three specific items are checked against their assigned spot at the end of the day, with a clear result for each.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Same as proficient, and the learner names a specific, reasoned change to the system based on what the test revealed.

lookFors: The chosen space and items are real and specific to the learner's actual household, not an invented example.
The one-day test report names actual items, not a general description of how organized the space feels.

A learner who completed the simulation/equal-credit alternative instead of the real-world version should be scored on this same rubric using the alternative submission as the evidence — using the sanctioned alternative is not itself a reason to score lower.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
